messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Design safe candidate isolation, verification, selection, and integration into a dirty shared repository.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

On conflict, set status CONFLICT and re-queue with the conflict diff prepended to the task context."],"failureModes":["Base SHA drifts: shared repo advances before integration, causing `git am` conflicts on a valid patch. Mitigation: before `git am`, rebase the worktree commit onto current HEAD and re-verify if the rebased diff delta exceeds a threshold.","Verifier learns producer context via a shared log sink or tmp directory, breaking independence. Mitigation: verifier subprocess launches with a clean environment, no worktree path access, stdout-only result channel.","Flaky tests cause a valid patch to fail verification. Mitigation: verifier re-runs the suite up to three times; a patch must fail all runs to be rejected, with per-run results stored in the verdict.","Stale worktrees accumulate after crashes. Mitigation: on every job claim, scan /tmp/candidate-* for entries whose job_id has no IN_PROGRESS record and prune them before creating the new worktree.","Repeated INTEGRATION_FAILED with no new context causes infinite re-queue loops. Mitigation: track `integration_attempt_count`; at count >= 3, set status HUMAN_REVIEW and stop re-queuing."],"successMetric":"Single-task round trip visible in the append-only job log: worktree created on claim, all producer writes confined to it, patch stored after commit, verifier verdict present with no producer context visible, `git am` applied to shared repo, post-integration tests green, worktree removed, job settled DONE — zero direct writes to the shared repo working tree during candidate production."}

structured_output.absentMechanism: The seed applies edits directly to the shared working tree with no per-candidate sandbox: one task, one agent, edits applied in place. There is no git-worktree isolation scoped to a verified-clean base commit, no verifier role distinct from the producer (the producer's own test run is the only gate), no multi-candidate scoring or selection, and no conflict-aware patch application back to a dirty shared repository. Any mid-task crash or parallel work leaves the shared tree in an undefined state with no rollback path.
design: Each claimed job shells out `git worktree add /tmp/candidate-<job_id> <last_verified_sha>` immediately on claim, forking from the last integration-verified commit, not from the current dirty working tree. The worktree path is written into the job record before any agent invocation.

The producing agent's file-write tool enforces a path prefix constraint: any write outside `job.worktree_path` returns an error and halts the edit loop. No other isolation mechanism is needed; the constraint is in the tool layer, not the model.

After the producer commits inside the worktree, `git -C <worktree_path> format-patch HEAD~1 --stdout` extracts the patch, stored in the job record as opaque bytes. The worktree is now read-only to the producer.

A separate verifier agent invocation receives only (task_spec, patch_bytes) — no producer reasoning trace, no shared filesystem path to the worktree. It applies the patch to a fresh copy of the worktree base, runs tests, and emits a structured verdict: `{pass: bool, test_counts: {pass, fail, skip}, static_violations: []}`.

When multiple candidates exist for one task, selection is deterministic: verified candidates rank by (test_pass_rate DESC, static_violations_count ASC, patch_line_count ASC); ties break by claim_timestamp ASC. Selection is a pure function over job records — no model call.

Integration applies the selected patch to the shared repo via `git am --3way <patch_bytes>`; on conflict the job transitions to CONFLICT state with the conflict diff appended to its context field and re-enters the work queue. The patch is never silently discarded.

A post-integration step re-runs the full test suite on the shared repo; failure triggers `git am --abort` and transitions to INTEGRATION_FAILED. After three such transitions, the job escalates to HUMAN_REVIEW with full failure history.
Worktrees are removed unconditionally via `git worktree remove --force` after integration success or failure. The patch bytes in the job record are the durable artifact; the directory is ephemeral.
firstVerticalSlice: Add `worktree_path: str | None` and `patch_bytes: bytes | None` to the job schema. On claim, run `git worktree add /tmp/candidate-{job_id} HEAD` and write the path into the job record before returning the job to the agent.
Wrap the existing file-write tool: reject any path not prefixed by `job.worktree_path` with a structured error. This enforces isolation without changing the agent's edit loop.

After the agent's existing commit step, run `git -C {worktree_path} format-patch HEAD~1 --stdout` and store the result in `job.patch_bytes`. Transition job status from IN_PROGRESS to AWAITING_VERIFICATION.

Invoke a second agent process with env vars `TASK_SPEC` and `PATCH_BYTES` only — no worktree path, no session state. It applies the patch, runs pytest, and writes a verdict JSON to stdout. The orchestrator reads and stores it in the job record.

On PASS verdict, run `git am --3way` in the shared repo. On success, settle job DONE and run `git worktree remove --force`. On conflict, set status CONFLICT and re-queue with the conflict diff prepended to the task context.
failureModes: Base SHA drifts: shared repo advances before integration, causing `git am` conflicts on a valid patch. Mitigation: before `git am`, rebase the worktree commit onto current HEAD and re-verify if the rebased diff delta exceeds a threshold.

Verifier learns producer context via a shared log sink or tmp directory, breaking independence. Mitigation: verifier subprocess launches with a clean environment, no worktree path access, stdout-only result channel.
Flaky tests cause a valid patch to fail verification. Mitigation: verifier re-runs the suite up to three times; a patch must fail all runs to be rejected, with per-run results stored in the verdict.
Stale worktrees accumulate after crashes. Mitigation: on every job claim, scan /tmp/candidate-* for entries whose job_id has no IN_PROGRESS record and prune them before creating the new worktree.
Repeated INTEGRATION_FAILED with no new context causes infinite re-queue loops. Mitigation: track `integration_attempt_count`; at count >= 3, set status HUMAN_REVIEW and stop re-queuing.
structured_output.successMetric: Single-task round trip visible in the append-only job log: worktree created on claim, all producer writes confined to it, patch stored after commit, verifier verdict present with no producer context visible, `git am` applied to shared repo, post-integration tests green, worktree removed, job settled DONE — zero direct writes to the shared repo working tree during candidate production.
